source_text: γʹ. Εἶδες, ἀγαπητὲ, οἰκονομίαν Θεοῦ, καὶ διὰ τῶν ἀπίστων καὶ τῶν πιστῶν τὰ καθ' ἑαυτὸν οἰκονομοῦντος, ἵνα μάθωσιν οἱ ἀλλότριοι τῆς εὐσεβείας τὴν ἰσχὺν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ὁ μὲν ἀστὴρ τοὺς μάγους ἤγαγεν ἀπὸ τῆς ἀνατολῆς, ὁ δὲ νόμος τὴν Μαριὰμ εἷλκεν ἐπὶ τὴν πατρίδα τὴν ὑπὸ τῶν προφητῶν εἰρημένην. Ἐντεῦθεν ἡμῖν δῆλόν ἐστιν, ὅτι καὶ ἡ Παρθένος ἐκ γένους ἐστὶ Δαυϊδικοῦ· ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἐκ τῆς Βηθλεὲμ ἦν, εὔδηλον ὅτι καὶ ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου καὶ τῆς πατριᾶς ἦν τοῦ Δαυΐδ. Τοῦτο καὶ ἀνωτέρω ἐδήλωσεν ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς, ἐν οἷς ἔλεγεν· Ἀνέβη δὲ καὶ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας σὺν Μαριὰμ, διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐξ οἴκου καὶ πατριᾶς Δαυΐδ. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ὁ μὲν Ἰωσὴφ ἐγενεαλογήθη, τοὺς δὲ ταύτης προγόνους οὐδεὶς ἡμῖν ἠρίθμησεν οὕτως, ὡς τοὺς ἐκείνου· ἵνα μὴ ἀμφιβάλλῃς καὶ λέγῃς, Πόθεν οὖν δῆλον, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ Δαυΐδ ἐστι καὶ αὐτή; ἄκουσον· Ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀπεστάλη ὁ ἄγγελος Γαβριὴλ ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ᾗ ὄνομα Ναζαρὲθ, πρὸς παρθένον μεμνηστευμένην ἀνδρὶ, ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰωσὴφ, ἐξ οἴκου Δαυΐδ. Τὸ, ἐξ οἴκου Δαυῒδ, περὶ τῆς Παρθένου ὑποληπτέον εἰρῆσθαι· ὅπερ οὖν καὶ ἐνταῦθα δεδήλωται. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ τὸ πρόσταγμα καὶ ὁ νόμος οὗτος ἐφοίτα, ἀνάγων ἐπὶ τὴν Βηθλεὲμ αὐτούς· ὁμοῦ τε γὰρ τῆς πόλεως ἐπέβησαν, καὶ Ἰησοῦς εὐθέως ἐτίκτετο. Διὸ καὶ ἐν φάτνῃ κατεκλίνετο, πολλῶν πανταχόθεν τότε συντρεχόντων, καὶ τοὺς τόπους προκαταλαμβανόντων, καὶ πολλὴν ποιούντων τὴν στενοχωρίαν· ὅθεν ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ μάγοι προσεκύνησαν. Ἵνα δὲ σαφεστέραν καὶ γνωριμωτέραν ὑμῖν ἀπόδειξιν παράσχωμαι, διανάστητέ μοι, παρακαλῶ, νῦν· καὶ γὰρ μακρὰν ἱστορίαν ἀνακινῆσαι βούλομαι, καὶ παλαιοὺς ἀναγνῶναι νόμους, ὥστε πάντοθεν ὑμῖν γενέσθαι τὸν λόγον σαφέστερον. Νόμος ἦν παλαιὸς τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις· μᾶλλον δὲ ἀνωτέρω τὸν λόγον ἀγάγωμεν· Ὅτε τῶν Αἰγυπτιακῶν θορύβων καὶ τῆς τοῦ βαρβάρου τυραννίδος τὸν τῶν Ἑβραίων δῆμον ἀπήλλαξεν ὁ Θεὸς, ὁρῶν αὐτοὺς ἔτι λείψανα ἀσεβείας ἔχοντας καὶ περὶ τὰ αἰσθητὰ ἐπτοημένους, καὶ μεγέθη καὶ κάλλη ναῶν θαυμάζον τας, ἐκέλευσεν αὐτοῖς οἰκοδομηθῆναι ναὸν, οὐχὶ τῇ πολυτελείᾳ τῆς ὕλης μόνον, οὐδὲ τῇ ποικιλίᾳ τῆς τέχνης, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ σχήματι τῆς οἰκοδομῆς πάντας τοὺς ἐν τῇ γῇ ναοὺς ἀποκρύπτοντα. Καὶ καθάπερ πατὴρ φιλόστοργος διὰ πολλοῦ χρόνου τὸν υἱὸν τὸν ἑαυτοῦ μιαροῖς ἀνθρώποις καὶ φθορεῦσι καὶ ἀσώτοις συναναστραφέντα καὶ πολλῆς ἀπολαύσαντα τρυφῆς λαβὼν, μετὰ ἀσφαλείας καὶ σεμνότητος ἐπὶ πλείονι καθίστησιν αὐτὸν ἀφθονίᾳ, ὥστε μήτε στενοχωρηθέντα τῶν προτέρων μνήμην λαβεῖν, μήτε εἰς ἐπιθυμίαν ἐκείνων ἐλθεῖν· οὕτω καὶ ὁ Θεὸς βλέπων τοὺς Ἰουδαίους περὶ τὰ αἰσθητὰ ἐπτοημένους, καὶ ἐν τούτοις πολλὴν ποιεῖται τὴν ὑπερβολὴν, ὥστε αὐτοὺς μηδέποτε εἰς ἐπιθυμίαν τῶν Αἰγυπτίων ἢ τῶν παρ' Αἰγυπτίοις ἐλθεῖν. Καὶ ποιεῖται τὸν ναὸν πρὸς τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ κόσμου παντὸς, τοῦ τε αἰσθητοῦ καὶ νοητοῦ. Καθάπερ γάρ ἐστι γῆ καὶ οὐρανὸς, καὶ μέσον διάφραγμα τὸ στερέωμα τοῦτο· οὕτω κἀκεῖνον ἐκέλευσε γενέσθαι. Καὶ εἰς δύο διατεμὼν τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον, καὶ καταπέτασμα ἀφεὶς μέσον, τὸ μὲν ἔξω τοῦ καταπετάσματος πᾶσι συνεχώρησεν εἶναι βατὸν, τὸ δὲ ἔνδον ἄβατον καὶ ἀθέατον πᾶσι, πλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως μόνου.
thought_title: God's plan draws Mary to Bethlehem and the temple mirrors the cosmos
orientation: Chrysostom is addressing the congregation, showing how God used both the star and the census law to bring the Magi and Mary to Bethlehem, and he is about to launch into a long explanation of the old Jewish temple as an image of the whole world.
pass_a_gloss: You saw, beloved, the plan of salvation of God, who arranges his own affairs through both the faithless and the faithful, so that those outside the faith may learn his strength and his power. And the star led the Magi from the east, but the law drew Mary to the homeland spoken of by the prophets. From this it is clear to us that the Virgin also is from the line of David; for since she was from Bethlehem, it is quite clear that she was also from the house and lineage of David. This the Evangelist also made clear earlier, in the words where he said: And Joseph also went up from Galilee with Mary, because he was of the house and lineage of David. For since Joseph was given a genealogy, but no one enumerated her ancestors to us in the way that they enumerated his; so that you may not doubt and say, From where then is it clear that she also is from David? listen: In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee, whose name was Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man, whose name was Joseph, of the house of David. The phrase, of the house of David, must be understood to have been said about the Virgin; which indeed has also been made clear here. For this reason both the decree and this law went forth, bringing them up to Bethlehem; for at the same time they entered the city, and Jesus was immediately born. For this reason also he was laid in a manger, since many were then running together from everywhere, and occupying the places beforehand, and making great the crowding; from which place the Magi also worshipped him there. But so that I may provide you a clearer and more recognizable proof, stand up for me, I ask, now; for I wish to stir up a long history, and to read old laws, so that the word may become clearer to you from every side. There was an old law for the Jews; but rather let us bring the word up higher: When God freed the people of the Hebrews from the Egyptian tumults and from the tyranny of the barbarian, seeing them still having remnants of impiety and being excited about sensible things, and marveling at the sizes and beauties of temples, he commanded a temple to be built for them, surpassing all the temples on the earth not only in the costliness of the material, nor only in the variety of the craftsmanship, but also in the form of the building. And just as a loving father, after a long time, taking his own son who had associated with defiled men and corrupters and profligates and had enjoyed much luxury, establishes him with safety and dignity in greater abundance, so that he may neither, being distressed, take memory of the former things, nor come into desire of those things; so also God, seeing the Jews excited about sensible things, makes in these things a great excess, so that they may never come into desire of the Egyptian things or of the things among the Egyptians. And he makes the temple according to the image of the whole world, both the sensible and the intelligible. For just as there is earth and heaven, and in the middle this firmament as a partition; so also he commanded that one to be made. And having cut this temple into two, and having let down a veil in the middle, he allowed the part outside the veil to be accessible to all, but the part inside to be inaccessible and unseen to all, except to the high priest alone.

choices.english: the plan of salvation of God
choices.why: Glossary requires 'plan of salvation' for οἰκονομία, and the genitive Θεοῦ is rendered as 'of God' to keep the source order and force.
The participle keeps the active sense of God managing his own matters; 'arranges' preserves the verbal force of οἰκονομέω without importing the banned noun.

choices.term: ἐπὶ τὴν πατρίδα τὴν ὑπὸ τῶν προφητῶν εἰρημένην
choices.english: to the homeland spoken of by the prophets
choices.why: Keeps the passive participle 'spoken of' and the agent 'by the prophets' in source order, preserving the emphasis on prophetic testimony.
rejected: to the fatherland mentioned by the prophets
to the ancestral city the prophets named

choices.why: Literal rendering of the fixed biblical phrase; 'house' is the standard English for οἶκος in genealogical contexts.
The verb ἀποκρύπτω here means to outshine or eclipse by comparison; 'surpassing' captures the comparative force of the temple exceeding all others.
Glossary requires 'veil' for καταπέτασμα, the curtain separating the Holy of Holies.

pass_b_english: Do you see, beloved, the plan of salvation of God, who arranges his own affairs through both the faithless and the faithful, so that those outside true religion may learn his strength and power? The star led the magi from the east, and the law drew Mary to the homeland spoken of by the prophets. From this it is clear to us that the Virgin also is of Davidic descent; for since she was from Bethlehem, it is obvious that she was also of the house and lineage of David. The Evangelist made this clear earlier when he said: And Joseph also went up from Galilee with Mary, because he was of the house and lineage of David (Luke 2:4). For Joseph's genealogy was traced, but no one enumerated her ancestors the way they did his. So that you may not doubt and say, "How then is it clear that she too is from David?" listen: In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David (Luke 1:26-27). The phrase "of the house of David" must be understood as spoken about the Virgin; and this very thing has been shown here as well. For this reason the decree and this law went out, bringing them up to Bethlehem. For as soon as they set foot in the city, Jesus was immediately born. Therefore he was also laid in a manger, since many people were rushing together from everywhere at that time, occupying the places beforehand and causing great crowding. That is where the magi worshiped him. But so that I may offer you a clearer and more recognizable proof, please stand up now; for I want to stir up a long history and read ancient laws, so that my word may become clearer to you from every side. There was an ancient law among the Jews. But let me take the account further back. When God delivered the Hebrew people from the Egyptian tumults and the tyranny of the barbarian, he saw that they still had remnants of impiety and were excited about material things, marveling at the size and beauty of temples. So he commanded them to build a temple that would surpass all the temples on earth, not only in the costliness of its materials and the variety of its craftsmanship, but also in the design of its structure. And just as a loving father, after a long time, takes back his son who has associated with defiled men, corrupters, and profligates, and who has enjoyed great luxury, and establishes him in greater abundance with security and dignity, so that he neither remembers his former life because of any lack nor longs for those things again—so also God, seeing the Jews excited about material things, lavishes great excellence upon these very things, so that they would never long for the things of the Egyptians or those among the Egyptians. And he makes the temple according to the image of the whole world, both the material and the spiritual. For just as there is earth and heaven, and this firmament as a partition in the middle, so he commanded that temple to be made. And dividing this temple into two, and placing a veil in the middle, he permitted the area outside the veil to be accessible to all, but the area inside to be inaccessible and unseen by all, except the high priest alone.

problems.quote: goes to great excess in these very things
problems.source_quote: ἐν τούτοις πολλὴν ποιεῖται τὴν ὑπερβολήν
problems.why: God makes great provision/excellence in these things, not 'goes to excess.'
problems.fix: lavishes great excellence upon these very things
problems.ruling: πολλὴν τὴν ὑπερβολὴν ποιεῖται means 'makes great excess/superiority,' not 'goes to excess'; 'excess' misrepresents God's deliberate provision as overindulgence.

edits.old: goes to great excess in these very things
edits.new: lavishes great excellence upon these very things

fixed: Changed 'goes to great excess in these very things' to 'lavishes great excellence upon these very things' because the source 'ἐν τούτοις πολλὴν ποιεῖται τὴν ὑπερβολήν' means God makes great provision/excellence in these things, not that he goes to excess.

last_rejected.why: The law drew Joseph and Mary, not Mary alone; 'αὐτούς' later confirms both were led.

last_rejected.ruling: ὁ δὲ νόμος τὴν Μαριὰμ εἷλκεν says the law drew Mary; later αὐτούς confirms both, but this sentence focuses on Mary.

last_rejected.quote: because he was of the house and lineage of David
last_rejected.source_quote: διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐξ οἴκου καὶ πατριᾶς Δαυΐδ
last_rejected.why: The Greek says 'because he [Joseph] was,' but the English could mislead; though contextually clear, the citation format obscures that this is the Evangelist's words about Joseph specifically.
last_rejected.fix: because he was of the house and lineage of David
last_rejected.ruling: διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν accurately renders 'because he was'; the English correctly preserves the Evangelist's words about Joseph.

last_rejected.quote: lavishes great excellence upon these very things
last_rejected.why: 'ὑπερβολὴν' means excess/superabundance, not 'excellence'; God makes the temple extravagantly splendid, not merely excellent.
last_rejected.fix: makes great excess in these very things
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπερβολή can mean 'excellence' or 'superabundance'; 'excellence' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: this firmament as a partition in the middle
last_rejected.why: 'τοῦτο' refers back to the temple structure being described, not 'this firmament'; the firmament itself is the partition.
last_rejected.fix: the firmament as a partition in the middle
last_rejected.ruling: τοῦτο refers to στερέωμα; 'this firmament as a partition' correctly identifies the firmament as the διάφραγμα.

last_rejected.quote: And he makes the temple according to the image of the whole world, both the material and the spiritual
last_rejected.source_quote: Καὶ ποιεῖται τὸν ναὸν πρὸς τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ κόσμου παντός, τοῦ τε αἰσθητοῦ καὶ νοητοῦ
last_rejected.why: Missing 'he' subject—God makes the temple; more importantly, 'ποιεῖται' is middle voice, 'he has the temple made' or 'he causes the temple to be made,' not directly 'he makes.'
last_rejected.fix: And he has the temple made according to the image of the whole world, both the visible and the intelligible
last_rejected.ruling: ποιεῖται middle voice can mean 'makes'; causative nuance is preference, not a major meaning change.
